description: ol-reserved-word (issue #837, maintainer ruling #833): DECLARING `mod` collides. `mod` is a word-spelled operator of the expression grammar rather than a callable primitive (spec/grammar.md:378), and it was the only one of the four (`and`/`or`/`not`/`mod`) missing from the keyword list, which is why `define mod` checked clean before #837 while `define and` already raised. Issue #838 removed the `namespace` param this fixture used to pin as `"reserved"`: spec/error-model.md:125,132-141 gives `ol-reserved-word` `params: { name }` only, because whether the taken name is a keyword, a primitive or an alias spelling "is an implementation distinction the learner never has to learn" -- so what makes `mod`'s membership visible now is that it is here at all, not a category label. Its token class is a separate, independent axis and does NOT change -- `mod` stays `operator`, exactly as `and` does, because spec/grammar.md:378 makes the `keyword` token class and the keyword list "different sets on purpose". Binding and calling `mod` are unaffected: keyword-mod-binds-and-calls-freely pins those. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) -- nothing is executed and no events are produced.
